notes: (b) ours: q^e divides every large highly abundant n. If v_q(n) < e infinitely often: (1) some fixed r with v_r unbounded -> m = n q^i/r^j, q^i < r^j < q^i(1+delta/2); (2) v_r bounded, largest prime P unbounded -> m = n q^i r^k/P with q^i r^k in (P/(1+delta/2), P); (3) else some other exponent unbounded, as (1). Each gives m < n with sigma(m) > sigma(n). (a) Eppstein 2015 blog case analysis (P < p^2 lemma), cited only. b-file check: last non-multiples of k = 2..49 listed in README. Outside Lean: all of (b); (a) entirely (Eppstein).
